title: Local frames from an ordinary etale identification
statement: Let S be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], F an algebraic space with its small etale site and structure sheaf [def-trf-algebraic-space], V an object of that site, N an F-module sheaf, and L an ordinary invertible module on the underlying scheme of V [def-sc-invertible-module]. Suppose e is an ordinary etale identification of L with N over V [def-sfb-ordinary-etale-identification]. For every site object T and arrow a:T to V, there is a covering sieve R on T such that for every arrow f:U to T in R, N restricted to the localized site over U is isomorphic to its structure module. There is no atlas, overlap datum, joint-surjectivity assumption, or assertion of global local freeness outside V.

source.place: Tag 05VG (lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent-properties), rank-one local frames; spaces-descent.tex Tag 060X.

proof.text: The ordinary pullback of L to the underlying scheme of T is invertible. Choose its Zariski trivializing opens. As scheme opens are etale, these give a jointly surjective etale covering of T, hence a covering in the small site. The same construction handles an empty T.

Over each trivializing open U and every further test W to U, pull back the ordinary frame, use the canonical tensor-unit comparison, and compose with e.app. Naturality of e and the unit-normalized composition maps make the linear equivalences and their inverses natural. Thus they give an isomorphism of module sheaves with the localized structure module. Every arrow of the generated covering sieve factors through a trivializing open, so pull back the same frame along that factorization.

source.place: Tags 03LC and 05VG; spaces-descent.tex Tag 060X, rank-one case

lean.statement:
theorem ordinary_etale_identification_local_frames
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (F : AlgebraicSpace S) (V : F.EtaleSite)
    (N : F.Modules) (L : (F.etaleForget.obj V).Modules)
    (hL : Scheme.Modules.IsInvertible L) (e : OrdinaryEtaleIdentification F V N L)
    (T : F.EtaleSite) (a : T ⟶ V) :
    ∃ R : Sieve T, R ∈ F.etaleTopology T ∧
      ∀ (U : F.EtaleSite) (f : U ⟶ T), R f →
        Nonempty ((F.etalePullback U).obj N ≅
          SheafOfModules.unit (F.structureSheaf.over U))
